Summary:
Quick orientation and handoff from AE to CSM/SE. Gathered infra constraints (VPC peering, egress rules), security checklist items (SOC2, KMS, SSO), clarified pilot scope (10k monthly queries, conversational agent + embeddings rerank), and agreed next steps: run perf checklist, share runbook, schedule pilot kickoff.

Transcript body:
[00:00] Maya (AE): Hey everyone, thanks for jumping on. Quick intro, I'm Maya, I'll be your AE, and with me are Liam (SE) and Priya (CSM). How's everyone doing?
[00:07] Daniel (Customer): Good, thanks. Busy week but ready.
[00:10] Sofia: Hi all, Sofia here from SecOps. We'll mostly listen but will ask the usual network/audit questions.
[00:16] Liam (SE): Awesome. I'll try not to talk in too many kernels and quant terms, promise.
[00:20] Janelle: Thanks. We wanted to make sure this is practical—timeline, who's doing what, and what blocks we should expect.
[00:30] Maya: Yep. Today's goal is to hand off the onboarding playbook, confirm pilots and success criteria, and surface any security or networking blockers. We'll capture action items and get a kickoff on the calendar.
[00:40] Daniel: Pilot scope — we said 10k queries/month, primarily conversational support and a reranker for ticket triage. Latency SLO is 500ms p50, 800ms p95 ideally. Cost should be reasonable; we're evaluating dedicated reserved vs hosted per-call.
[00:56] Maya: Great, that's consistent. Liam, any immediate notes on that workload?
[01:00] Liam: Yep, conversational plus rerank is a typical pattern. For 10k/month that's not huge, but p95 matters. We usually recommend a dedicated pool for consistent latency, but caching and prefix caching can make hosted acceptable if you want to start fast.
[01:18] Ravi (Customer): Quick question — by dedicated, do you mean Redwood Dedicated with a reserved GPU pool? We have constraints on bringing more hosts into our VPC.
[01:25] Liam: Correct; dedicated means reserved capacity in an isolated tenant. For Private deployment, we can do VPC peering or on-prem, but that'll add network ops and a longer lead time.
[01:36] Sofia: From SecOps: we need SOC2 artifacts, the KMS/HSM model, SSO integration (SAML/Okta), and logging/retention policies. Also clarify whether traffic traverses public internet during served inference or if egress is within peered links.
[01:53] Priya (CSM): We'll pull the SOC2 summary and the network diagram. Maya, I'll sync with product docs to get the KMS integration notes.
[02:00] Maya: Yep, I'll attach the security pack. Also note that some of the product names in our docs get mangled by the recorder — e.g., "Redwood Dedicated" sometimes shows up as "Roodwood Dedicate" — just ignore that in the auto notes.
[02:15] Janelle: Haha noted.
[02:20] Daniel: For networking, our infra team needs the specific IP ranges for peering, and an expected pattern of egress endpoints. We also have strict egress rules — no unknown external connections.
[02:31] Liam: We'll provide a minimal set of endpoints and a CIDR range for peering. For hosted, you'll see outbound calls to model artifacts during startup unless you pin a model and use an image-based approach. For Dedicated or Private, artifacts can be cached in region to reduce that.
[02:50] Ravi: How about audit logs? We need to know retention granularity and whether we can forward to our SIEM.
[02:55] Priya: Yes, audit logs can be forwarded to your Splunk/Datadog via syslog or S3 ingestion; retention windows are configurable by plan. We'll include a sample retention policy in the runbook.
[03:10] Sofia: KMS — do you support customer-managed keys? We have compliance people that insist on CMKs and HSMs.
[03:16] Liam: Yes, CMK supported via our KMS integration, though for Private on-prem you'll have direct HSM options. For hosted, there's envelope encryption with CMKs available on enterprise tiers. I'll forward the KMS integration matrix.
[03:28] Daniel: Timeline question — what does a typical pilot look like? 2–4 weeks?
[03:31] Maya: Typical pilot is 2–6 weeks depending on benchmarks. For you I'd recommend a 3-week pilot: week 1 infra & network setup, week 2 baseline perf & small live traffic, week 3 tuning and runbook for cutover.
[03:45] Janelle: Would you recommend starting hosted to iterate faster, then move to dedicated? Or do dedicated up front?
[03:50] Liam: Both valid. If you have tight security constraints, start with dedicated or Private. If you want speed and less ops, hosted can prove the workload quickly; then move to dedicated for consistent p95. We'll lay out cost delta in the runbook.
[04:05] Maya: I'll send a matrix comparing hosted vs dedicated vs private with cost ballparks and lead times.
[04:12] Ravi: Regarding data residency — any concerns if we host in us-east vs eu-west? We're primarily US.
[04:17] Priya: We'll default to us-east but if you need EU-only region we can flag that. For dedicated we can pin region.
[04:24] Daniel: Who owns the rollbacks and runbooks during cutover? We need a clear on-call and runbook ops owner.
[04:30] Priya: CS will own the runbook/ops play and work with your on-call. We'll document escalation paths and a canary rollback plan.
[04:40] Maya: Great — any blockers we haven't captured?
[04:44] Sofia: One more from SecOps: certification of the deployment — do you do annual pentests or provide third-party attestations?
[04:51] Liam: We have third-party pen test reports for the hosted plane and we can share SOC2 Type II summary. For private/on-prem, customer is responsible for their environment's pentest, but we can provide guidance.
[05:05] Daniel: Good. Ok, let's talk about the runbook contents briefly.
[05:08] Maya: Runbook will include: pre-req checklist, VPC peering steps, firewall rules, SSO setup steps, KMS config, model pinning and cache config, benchmarking checklist, and escalation matrix.
[05:20] Liam: Benchmark checklist — we'll measure cold start p50/p95, token throughput, KV cache hit rates, and end-to-end request latency with typical prompt sizes. Also we want a sampling of prompt sets to check hallucination regressions.
[05:36] Janelle: On hallucination monitoring — we need a plan to validate outputs against curations. Does Redwood have an eval harness?
[05:41] Priya: Yes, Redwood Optimize has evaling and regression alerts tied to prompt sets. We'll include an example harness in the repo.
[05:50] Daniel: Great, can we see a sample cost breakdown for the pilot vs production?
[05:54] Maya: Yes, I'll include a simple spreadsheet: pilot costs, expected per 1M tokens, cost delta between quant profiles, and dedicated commit pricing.
[06:05] Ravi: Any legal red flags for procurement? We've to loop in procurement for contract terms and data processing addenda.
[06:12] Maya: We'll get the DPA and standard contract template; procurement will handle SSO/SCs. I'll cc legal as needed.
[06:20] Sofia: Can we get an architecture diagram that shows where logs live and where keys are held?
[06:25] Liam: Absolutely, that will be in the security pack.
[06:30] Maya: Recap of next steps: I will send the runbook and pricing by 9/10, Liam will prepare the perf checklist by 9/15, Priya to schedule pilot kickoff for 9/13, and Daniel to send network constraints by 9/11.
[06:45] Janelle: Perfect. Thanks everyone.
[06:48] Daniel: Thanks all.
[06:50] Maya: We'll follow up with calendar invites and the docs. End meeting.

Notes about transcription: occasional mis-hearings — e.g., "KV cache" transcribed as "K V cache"; "SOC 2" sometimes appears as "sock two". Speaker labels auto-assigned, may not reflect exact corporate titles.
